lines.en: So, how did you know Frances?
Well, actually, I really -- I hadn't seen her for years.
But, um, well, I was pretty tight with her and her daughter.
Really? What's your name?
Frank Bouffet.
Oh.
You know, let's strike that.
My name, uh, actually is Joe.
Uh, Joe, uh, Hill.
You're Frank Bouffet?
Shh! No! Joe Hill!
But you just said --
You know what? I gotta go.
And thank you so much for coming.
Did you catch up?
Uh-huh.
Oh, what did he say?
He said, um, "Nice to meet you, Glenda."
Well, obviously, I couldn't give him my real name.
Why? Why not?
Come on, you saw the way he ran out of here.
What do you think, he's gonna stick around
and talk to the daughter he abandoned?
What did you say to him?
Well, I -- I told him that, you know,
I was the executor person of Frances's will
and that I needed to talk to him.
So, I'm gonna meet him at the coffee house later.
You -- and, uh, you were married to Frances's daughter, Lily.
Is that correct?
Yes. Yes, I was.
Okay. Um, question two.
Um, did that marriage end, A, happily,
B, medium, or C, in the total abandonment
of her and her two children?
It really says that?
Yeah, C.
Well, I guess then I -- I would -- I would have to say C.
Oh, okay.
Total abandonment.
Uh-huh.
Okay. Reasons for abandonment.
Um, A, top secret government work.
B, amnesia.
Or C, you're just a selfish, irresponsible, bad, bad man.
You know, I don't think I want the lipstick that much.
But, uh, oh, would you do me a favor?
And, um, would you -- would you give Lily that, please?
What?
Well, Lily, when you see Lily, would you give her that -- that note?
Because I wanted to talk to her at the memorial.
But, well, I pictured her getting mad at me
the way you got mad at me.
And I -- I chickened out.
So, uh, I wrote her that note.
Would you give it to her, please?
But you -- you -- you came to see Lily?
Yeah. Yeah. Why?
Lily's dead.
She -- What?
She's dead.
Are you sure?
Well, if she isn't cremating her, it was a big mistake.
I can't believe this.
I just -- I can't believe -- how -- how -- oh, my God.
How -- how long ago?
17 years ago.
Oh.
What -- what about the girls?
Well, Ursula is a waitress.
And -- and she lives in Soho.
And Phoebe is on this couch.
And she lives in Soho.
Yep. Lipstick and a daughter.
Big day for you.
Oh, my God.
I -- I -- I -- I -- um, whoops.
I -- I -- I -- I don't know what -- I don't know what to say.
I just can't believe that you're my daughter.
You're so pretty.
Yes. Well, it's neither here nor there.
So would it -- would it make you feel better if I said that I was very, very sorry I left?
You know what? It doesn't matter what you say. It's not gonna make a difference anyway. So you can just go.
All right. Well, you know, in my defense, I was a lousy father.
- That's your defense? - Yes, it is. I burned the formula and I put your diapers on backwards.
I mean, I made up a -- a song to sing you to sleep, but that made you cry even more.
You make up songs?
Well, no, just -- just that one. But it was stupid.
Uh, let's see. How did it -- how did it go? Um, yeah. Okay.
S -- uh, "Sleepy girl, sleepy girl, why won't you go to sleep?"
"Sleepy girl, sleepy girl, you're -- you're -- you're -- you're keeping me up."
Uh, yeah.
I just -- I -- you know, I'm -- I'm not very good at this, so, um...
Well, I am.
Not yet. No.
